title: Council: How to Grow AOM
summary: Council brief on new business strategies and revenue growth opportunities.
content:
Council Brief -- How to Grow AOM From Here

Date: 2026-03-10 Agents present: Alex (Strategy), Jacob (Outreach), Bobby (Tech), Mom (Operations), Paige (Clients), Steffen (Brand) Question: What else can AOM do to bring in new business and grow revenue from this point?

Alex (Strategy/Offers)

Highest ROI moves, ranked:

  1. Close what's already warm. NEON, PA-LA, Intelliplay are sitting unsigned. Send a "checking in, booking Q2 now" follow-up. Cheapest revenue dollars you'll ever get.

  2. Upsell Ambition and KOHRS. Push Ambition to $3.5k once posting starts. After KOHRS backlog clears, pitch $3k tier with LinkedIn added. Gets recurring from $4k to $6.5-7k/month.

  3. $3k is too low for the floor. Structure tiers: $3k base (content only), $4.5k with video shoots, $6k full service. Most will land at $4.5k.

  4. Included Health is a case study, not just a project. Build a 60-second highlight reel after wrapping. Use it in outreach. Jacob should have a separate sequence for corporate event planners.

  5. AI advisory is NOT ready to sell. No defined deliverable, no case study, no price. Park it until Q2. When ready: "AI Operations Audit" at $2,500 flat, 2-week engagement, written report.

  6. Ash needs to be a revenue contributor. If Ash can run shoots solo, Patrik gets 2-3 hours back for sales.

Focus outreach on: Construction 10-50 employees with active Instagram (they already value social). Secondary: corporate event teams (the IH profile). Drop founders/nonprofits from cold outreach for now.

The one thing that changes everything: 2 more construction retainers at $4.5k average in 60 days = $9k/month new recurring. $13-16k/month steady. $250k+ annual run rate.

Jacob (Outreach/Market)

The math on cold email alone: 8-10/day, even 3% reply rate = 1 reply every 3-4 days. 20-30% close rate on cold replies = ~1 deal/month. Email works but it's a slow burn.

Four things to add alongside email:

  1. LinkedIn DMs. Tony sends 5-10 connection requests/day synced with Jacob's email list. Warms them up before email lands.

  2. In-person networking. One appearance at NAIOP, AZ Builders Alliance, or local BNI generates more leads in a morning than a month of cold email. Construction is a handshake industry.

  3. Referral asks. Ambition, KOHRS, Brandon Wiley are all construction-adjacent. "Who else in your world could use what we're doing for you?" Converts at 10-20x cold outreach.

  4. Case study content as magnet. Ambition before/after video on LinkedIn with Phoenix construction hashtags. Proves the work AND attracts inbound.

Phoenix market signal: Construction GCs and mechanical contractors are underserved on social. Most have zero LinkedIn, terrible websites, no video. The need is obvious but they don't know they need it. They need to SEE the result first. Ambition case study is the conversion tool.

Realistic timeline: First closed deal in 3-5 weeks from cold email. With LinkedIn + referrals + one local event, compress to 2-3 weeks.

Bobby (Tech/Web)

The site isn't closing deals because it's not built to.

Build priority order:

  1. CTA intake flow (this week). Multi-step form: What's your business? What do you need? Budget range? Captures leads at 11pm on a Tuesday. Highest-leverage thing to ship.

  2. Vertical landing pages. One for construction, one for small businesses. "Your competitors are posting and you're not. Here's what $3k/month gets you." Gives Jacob specific URLs for outreach.

  3. Case studies section. Ambition launches Thursday = instant shippable case study. Before/after. What we built. What it costs monthly.

  4. AI services: not a page, just a tile. Single "AI Audit" offer on services page. One thing, one price, one outcome.

  5. /outreach-plan as sales demo. Anonymize slightly. "This is what we built for ourselves. We can build it for you."

What NOT to do: Redesign (it looks good), blog (premature), client portal (solve "get clients" before "manage clients at scale").

Mom (Operations)

The hard truth: AOM is not at capacity. Patrik is at capacity.

Every new project requiring Patrik competes with Skylar, KOHRS, ISA, and Brandon for the same 4-5 evening editing blocks. And those blocks aren't happening consistently.

The bottleneck is editing. Full stop.

  1. Split editing between Patrik and Ash. No budget for a hire right now. Instead, divide the editing backlog by ownership:

    • Ash owns: KOHRS videos (already on it), routine social cuts, any footage that doesn't need Patrik's creative eye
    • Patrik owns: Skylar music video, ISA Energy brand video, Brandon documentary, Michael edit, anything that needs his creative direction
    • Rule: If Ash can do 80% of it, Ash does 100% of it. Patrik only touches edits that require his vision. This frees Patrik's evenings for closing deals instead of cutting KOHRS demo footage.
    • Weekly handoff: Sunday night, Patrik drops Ash a list of what needs editing that week. Ash confirms what he can take. No ambiguity about who owns what.

  2. Ship what's done before chasing what's new. Ambition launches Thursday = case study + referral source. KOHRS backlog must clear so Leigh doesn't churn.

  3. March $50k math. ~$35k through Jan/Feb. IH $9k + Ambition $4k web + KOHRS $2k = potentially $47-50k if IH pays in March. The W-9 reply is literally the most valuable 2-minute task.

  4. Push NEON, deprioritize PA-LA and Intelliplay. One follow-up call this week.

  5. Let Jacob run. Pipeline builds without Patrik's time. But when responses come, Patrik needs to be available for calls, not buried in a Resolve timeline.

  6. NABI: shelf it. Client isn't committed. Revisit Q2.

The growth answer isn't "do more." It's "stop doing the wrong things." Patrik on sales calls = $9k projects. Patrik editing KOHRS footage = $2k minus everything he didn't close that week.

Paige (Client Health)

Biggest risk: KOHRS. 10 videos behind while client pays $2k/month. Construction is referral-heavy. One unhappy client poisons the whole vertical strategy. Acknowledge the gap to Leigh directly. Give her a real timeline.

Highest upside: Included Health. Big company, multiple departments, multiple events per year. Post-delivery ask to Elario: "Who else on your team does events like this?" One warm intro = $30-50k/year in repeat work. Do NOT let this become a one-off.

Ambition = the proof case. Once launched, every construction pitch references what we built for them. Real results from a real contractor beats ten portfolio thumbnails.

NABI: let it go. Don't invest cycles rallying investors for a client who isn't committed.

Unsigned proposals need a deadline: "We're booking Q2 now, want to hold space if you're moving forward." If no response in a week, move to dead.

Referrals nobody's asked for yet:

  • Ambition's owner knows other contractors. After launch, ask directly.
  • Included Health's team post-delivery.
  • Brandon Wiley runs a business, knows business owners. Has anyone asked?

Fastest path to new business: Deliver so well for Ambition and IH that they refer you. Closes come from proof, not promises.

Steffen (Brand)

The visual identity is premium. The copy is the ceiling.

Design says "we work with serious people." Copy says "we work with construction companies." That's limiting.

Positioning fix: Industry-agnostic language, industry-specific proof.

Hero/value props should never name a single vertical. Instead:

  • "Companies that build things" (works for construction, founders, nonprofits)
  • "You're ahead of market. We make sure everyone else knows it."

Let case studies do the vertical targeting. Brand stays wide, proof narrows.

Missing brand assets:

  1. Case studies with numbers. Not "we made a video." Before/after with real results.
  2. Sizzle reel. 60-90 seconds, cinematic. Every $9k+ production company has one. Pull from ISA, Ambition, KOHRS footage.
  3. Social proof on site. Testimonials, client logos, "trusted by" names.

AI as positioning, not a service page yet. "We don't just produce content. We built the system that produces it." No other Phoenix production company can say that.

Kill "$9k in projects." Replace with "X projects delivered" or "clients across construction, energy, and nonprofits."

Differentiation language:

  • Not "we shoot video." Instead: "We build the thing that brings you business."
  • Not "social media management." Instead: "Your brand, showing up consistently, without you thinking about it."

Synthesis

Where everyone agrees:

  • Ambition launch Thursday is the #1 growth catalyst. It becomes the case study, the referral source, and the proof for every future pitch.
  • Included Health is the highest-upside relationship. Don't let it die as a one-off. Ask for internal referrals post-delivery.
  • KOHRS is the biggest risk. Fix the backlog before it becomes a reputation problem.
  • Cold email works but isn't enough alone. Add referral asks, LinkedIn DMs, and one in-person networking touchpoint.
  • NABI: shelf it. Don't chase reluctant money.
  • The site needs to convert, not just impress. Intake flow + case studies + vertical pages.
  • Copy needs to widen. Construction-forward is fine in proof/case studies, but hero and value props should speak to all verticals.

The big disagreement:

  • Alex says drop founders/nonprofits from outreach. Steffen says keep the brand wide. Resolution: Keep brand language inclusive, but focus outreach dollars and Jacob's time on construction. Founders/nonprofits come through the wide net (site, referrals, inbound).

The bottleneck (Mom called it):

  • Patrik is the closer, creative director, AND primary editor. Editing is fulfillment, not growth. Every hour editing is an hour not closing. Solution: split editing with Ash. Ash takes KOHRS, routine cuts, and anything that doesn't need Patrik's creative eye. Patrik keeps Skylar, ISA, Brandon, Michael. Weekly Sunday handoff keeps it clean.

Top 5 moves, in order:

  1. Ask existing clients for referrals (Ambition, IH post-delivery, Brandon). Zero cost, highest conversion.
  2. Split editing backlog with Ash. Weekly handoff system. Ash owns routine, Patrik owns creative. Frees Patrik's evenings for sales.
  3. Launch Ambition Thursday, then build the case study immediately. 60-second walkthrough for outreach and LinkedIn.
  4. Follow up on NEON this week. Soft deadline: "booking Q2 now."
  5. Bobby: build CTA intake flow on AOM site. Captures leads 24/7.

Recommended next action:

Everything can start running now. Referral asks cost nothing. Ash editing split starts this week. Bobby queued for CTA intake flow after Ambition launches.

Patrik's Decisions (Mar 10)

  1. Pricing: $3k feels high for cold outreach. Keep as starting point, may test lower entry ($2k content-only) and upsell.
  2. Ash shoots solo: Yes, and he does. Conferences require multiple people. Ash owns KOHRS (he brought it in).
  3. NEON follow-up: YES. Pitched show ideas early Feb, was going to circle back. Do it this week.
  4. Referral asks: NOT NOW. Need to finish delivering for those clients first.
  5. Ash editing schedule: Trying to find one. Hard to get Ash to execute on editing specifically. Needs structured accountability (recurring calendar blocks with specific deliverables).
